summary.name: Object Animation, a supplemental design reference not directly named in the source collection. Photographed object animation must be distinguished from digital simulation.
summary.visualIdentity: Everyday objects carry the subject while keeping their material, scale, and contact shadows. Motion comes from incremental movement, rotation, arrangement, and replacement, with objects related to each other. The intended method is photographed poses under fixed lighting and camera settings.
summary.suitableUses: Explicitly stated uses: playful product moments alone, data explainers with supplied figures (paired with style-097), and music-led product promos or social loops (paired with style-105). Inferred: explaining quantities through countable objects where each object equals one stated unit.
summary.limitations: Objects must not all move together without a relationship. Simulated motion must not be presented as photographed animation. Real objects are never recolored, values are never invented, and scales must not mislead. Lighting flicker and live audio drift must be avoided.
summary.palette: This is an optional, reference-dependent example applying only to new presentation elements; task or brand colors override it. Tokens: background #F1E9DD, foreground #3B423E, accent #8D8977. Foreground text on background measures 8.571 contrast, meeting the 4.5 target. Text on the accent fails at 2.937, so the accent is decorative only. Gradients are disabled, and source object colors stay unchanged.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Motion is incremental, with clear trajectories and readable held states. Delivery frame rate may exceed the planned pose exposure rate. Automatic springs, bounce, or extra in-between poses are not added. The style itself specifies no interaction. Optional pattern references are scroll chaptering, scroll storytelling, and cursor orbit, but the orbit requires real 3D depth or a labeled parallax alternative.
summary.audio: Audio is unspecified by the style and must be proposed per topic. Options include restrained contact or transition sound accents, ambience, beat-synchronized music, or silence. Speech must stay intelligible and must not compete with narration. Inferred: short contact sounds may suit photographed objects, but this is not stated by the source.
summary.assetRequirements: Required inputs are prepared photographed object frames or layers with transparency, consistent dimensions, clear naming, and a layer manifest or numbered sequence. Assets must be inspected before composition, and fonts and assets must load before rendering. Source photographs and product artwork remain unchanged. Any missing assets must be stated explicitly.
summary.combinations: Stated combinations: style-097 for data meaning with flat labels, and style-105 for beat-timed object moves. Optional pattern references are motion-012 and motion-015 for chaptered or narrative scenes. Motion-021 requires real 3D depth. Conflicting progress drivers between nested patterns must be avoided.
summary.productionApproach: HyperFrames is the default composition and export framework, with Remotion only as a documented fallback when HyperFrames cannot meet a constraint. Pillow handles crop and frame normalization, and FFmpeg encodes frame sequences. GSAP provides a paused, seekable timeline, and chroma-js only validates colors. The style renderer owns visuals, the motion engine owns trajectories, and the pipeline only composes and exports. Delivery requires frame and audio checks.
